title: Dominique Strauss-Kahn resigns as IMF Managing Director
trigger: Strauss-Kahn was arrested in New York on charges of sexual assault of a hotel housekeeper, leading him to resign as Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund.

timeline.event: Strauss-Kahn arrested at JFK Airport and charged with sexual assault of a hotel housekeeper
Strauss-Kahn resigns as IMF Managing Director, effective immediately
Christine Lagarde named as new IMF Managing Director
Criminal charges against Strauss-Kahn are dropped after prosecutors question the accuser's credibility

outcome.summary: Strauss-Kahn resigned from the IMF in May 2011 following his arrest. The criminal case was later dropped in August 2011 after prosecutors determined the accuser's credibility was compromised. He reached a civil settlement with the accuser in 2012. Christine Lagarde succeeded him as IMF Managing Director.

claims.text: Strauss-Kahn was arrested at JFK Airport on May 14, 2011 and charged with sexual assault
Strauss-Kahn resigned as IMF Managing Director on May 18, 2011
Christine Lagarde was appointed as Strauss-Kahn's successor at the IMF
Criminal charges were dropped on August 23, 2011 after prosecutors questioned the accuser's credibility
